title: Simplex Geometry: Grid-to-Real Embedding
content: `gridToReal v` maps a grid vertex v = (v₀,...,v_{d-1}) with integer coordinates summing to ≤ N to the point v/N in the standard d-simplex. The standard d-simplex Δᵈ = {x ∈ ℝᵈ : xᵢ ≥ 0, Σxᵢ ≤ 1} is encoded as `InSimplex d`. The lemma `gridToReal_inSimplex` proves this embedding is valid: the coordinates are non-negative (by division), and they sum to at most 1 (using `v.valid`: the integer coordinates sum to at most N). This geometric setup is dimension-independent — the proof works for any d.
mathContext: $\Gamma_N^d = \{v \in \mathbb{Z}^d : v_i \geq 0, \sum_i v_i \leq N\}$. Map: $v \mapsto v/N \in \Delta^d = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : x_i \geq 0, \sum x_i \leq 1\}$.

title: Barycentric Displacement: The Key Quantity
content:
The `baryDisp f v k` function measures how much the k-th barycentric coordinate changes when applying f at the grid point v. The standard d-simplex has d+1 barycentric coordinates λ₀,...,λ_d with Σλᵢ = 1 (where λ_d = 1 - Σ_{i<d} xᵢ is implicit). For k < d: d_k = f(v/N)_k - (v/N)_k (the explicit change). For k = d: d_d = -(Σ d_k for k < d) (to maintain the sum-to-zero constraint).

The critical lemma `baryDisp_sum_zero` proves Σ_{k=0}^d d_k = 0. This is the algebraic heart of the construction: because f maps Δ to Δ and the target has barycentric coordinates summing to 1, the net change in all barycentric coordinates sums to zero. The Lean proof uses `Fin.sum_univ_castSucc` to split the last term, then simplifies using the definitions.
mathContext: $d_k(f,v) = \lambda_k(f(v/N)) - \lambda_k(v/N)$. Sum: $\sum_{k=0}^d d_k(f,v) = 0$ since $\sum \lambda_k = 1$ for both $f(v/N)$ and $v/N$.

title: The Displacement Coloring: argmin of Barycentric Displacement
content:
The `displacementColoring hN f` assigns each grid vertex v a color `minIndex (baryDisp f v)` — the index k of the most negative barycentric displacement d_k. The auxiliary `minIndex` function (choosing the argmin of a finite function on Fin(n+1)) is noncomputable but well-defined via `Finset.exists_min_image`. The key property used is `minIndex_le`: the chosen index achieves the minimum, i.e., d_{minIndex} ≤ d_j for all j.

This single-line definition encodes the entire Brouwer-via-Sperner strategy. The intuition: if some coordinate of f(p) lags behind p (negative displacement), we assign that coordinate as the color. A fully-colored simplex is a simplex where every coordinate 'lags' at some vertex — indicating a near-fixed-point.

title: Proving the Sperner Condition: Three Supporting Lemmas
content:
The main theorem `displacementColoring_isSperner` is proved using three supporting lemmas:

1. `baryDisp_nonneg_on_face_lt` (k < d): On face k, vertex v has coordinate v_k = 0, so v/N has k-th coordinate 0. Since f maps to the simplex, f(v/N)_k ≥ 0. Therefore d_k = f(v/N)_k - 0 ≥ 0.

2. `baryDisp_nonneg_on_face_last` (k = d): On face d, Σv_i = N, so the last barycentric coordinate of v/N is 1 - Σ(v_i/N) = 0. Since f maps to the simplex, Σf(v/N)_i ≤ 1, giving d_d = -(Σd_k for k<d) = (1 - Σf_i) ≥ 0.

3. `exists_neg_baryDisp`: When f(v) ≠ v, the displacements are not all zero but sum to 0, so some must be negative. The clever Lean proof: assume all ≥ 0 (by contradiction), sum all non-negative values summing to 0 → all are 0 → f(v) = v, contradiction.

The main theorem combines these: on face k, d_k ≥ 0; since f(v) ≠ v, some d_j < 0; argmin ≤ d_j < 0 ≤ d_k means argmin ≠ k.
mathContext: Sperner condition: $c(v) \neq k$ when $v$ is on face $k$. Proof: $d_k(f,v) \geq 0$ on face $k$, but $d_{c(v)} = \min_j d_j \leq d_j < 0 \leq d_k$, so $c(v) \neq k$.

title: Brouwer FPT: Infrastructure, Approximate FPs, and Compactness
content:
The final section bridges the combinatorial result (Sperner + displacement) to Brouwer's theorem. `fsimplex_gridToReal_dist` bounds the L∞ diameter of any FSimplex by 1/N — the standard Lebesgue number argument. As N → ∞, the mesh diameter 1/N → 0.

`approximate_fixed_point` applies Sperner's lemma with the displacement coloring to get a fully-colored FSimplex at each refinement level N. The vertices of this simplex are within 1/N of each other and within 1/N of a near-fixed-point. By uniform continuity of f on the compact simplex, for large enough N the displacement bounds transfer, giving ε-approximate fixed points.

`brouwer_simplex` extracts the exact fixed point: the sequence of ε_N-approximate fixed points has a convergent subsequence (by sequential compactness of the compact simplex), and the limit satisfies f(x) = x by continuity. This is the standard compactness argument that converts approximate to exact fixed points.
mathContext: Mesh diameter: $\operatorname{diam}(\text{FSimplex with N}) \leq \sqrt{d}/N \to 0$. Brouwer: $\{x_N : |f(x_N) - x_N| < 1/N\}$ is a sequence in compact $\Delta^d$; any cluster point is a fixed point.
